title: Token-adaptive dequantization policy and blockwise kernel sparsifier for low-latency quantized paths
author: Marisol Vega
description:
Context: Certain customer workloads with short-lived contexts (conversation turns, search rerank slices) are sensitive to per-request dequant overhead. Existing dequant fusion paths for INT8/FP8 reduce operator count but still incur per-token memory traffic when invoked indiscriminately across batches.

Motivation: Reduce tail latency and average per-token cost by making the dequantization decision token-adaptive and by introducing a blockwise sparsification pass that lets kernels skip dense dequant work on low-importance token blocks. This PR implements a runtime policy and accompanying kernel-side fastpath that cooperates with KV-cache-aware continuous batching and scheduler heuristics.

Summary of changes: 1) Token-adaptive dequantization policy: a lightweight scoring function (based on token position, attention weight variance, and runtime quality heuristics collected at warmup) that marks token ranges as "hot" or "cold" for full dequantization. Hot ranges follow the existing fused dequant+matmul path; cold ranges use a reduced-precision in-place cast with deferred requant/rescale downstream. 2) Blockwise kernel sparsifier: new block-skipping annotations in the fused attention and FFN kernels to bypass dequant memory copies on contiguous low-importance blocks, implemented as an inline conditional in CUDA/TVM kernels to avoid extra dispatch overhead. 3) KV-cache integration: extend KV cache metadata to carry per-key block importance vectors; continuous batching aggregator uses these vectors to coalesce requests with similar block profiles to increase coalescing efficiency. 4) Scheduler hints: add "dequant_cost" and "block_sparsity" hints to the request router so the policy can prefer lanes that minimize latency SLO impact (e.g., route cold-block-heavy requests to high-throughput nodes). 5) Perf harness & benchmarks: new microbenchmarks and a production-style benchmark harness that simulates mixed-turn chat workloads to measure latency P50/P95 and token throughput under realistic batching.

Commits summary:
- feat(runtime): add token-adaptive-dequant policy and scoring utils
- feat(kernels): add blockwise sparsifier primitive and CUDA kernel patch
- perf(tests): add mixed-turn benchmark harness and scripts
- ci: add perf job to run harness on push

Changed areas/files (high-level):
- runtime/dequant_policy.py (new): main scoring logic and runtime config hooks
- runtime/scheduler/hints.py: add dequant_cost/block_sparsity hint plumbing
- serving/kv/metadata.proto: extend KV metadata with block importance vector (backwards-compatible optional field)
- kernels/attn/block_sparsifier.cu: block-skip implementation with inline fastpath
- kernels/ffn/block_sparsifier.cu: mirrored logic for FFN path
- kernels/fuse/dequant_fuse_pass.cc: tie-in for fused vs deferred path selection
- benchmarks/mixed_turn/README.md and harness scripts
- tests/unit/test_dequant_policy.py: coverage for scoring edge cases
- docs/ops/dequant_tuning.md: operator-level tuning knobs

Illustrative snippet (kernel guard): "if (unlikely(block_importance[i] < sparsity_threshold)) { // fast-skip dequant path; operate in-place with reduced copy } else { // full fused dequant+matmul }"

Review conversation:
- Siddharth Rao (reviewer): "Overall good direction; two concerns: 1) scoring should avoid oscillation across batches (we need hysteresis), 2) ensure metrics emitted for block-level quality so we can detect regressions."
- Marisol (author): "Added a 3-step exponential smoothing for scoring in dequant_policy.py and emitted block_quality metrics (histogram + tag by model/version)."
- Linnea Olsson: "Kernel looks solid but please add a fallback that disables skipping when debug flags enabled; also add comments explaining the alignment assumptions for block boundaries."
- Marisol: "Added debug flag and comments; updated unit tests to cover misaligned blocks."
- Ethan Brooks: "Bench numbers look promising but CI perf job failed on first run (OOM on small runner). Reran on bigger runner and results stable."

CI checks and timeline:
- Linux unit tests: pass
- Linter: pass
- CUDA kernel compile: pass
- Perf harness (initial): fail (OOM on small runner) -> rerun: pass (on large runner)
- Integration: pass

Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2024-11-18 by Marisol after approvals from Siddharth and Linnea. Rationale: performance gains without functional changes; opt-in runtime flag allows gradual rollout.

Measured results (benchmark harness, mixed-turn chat profile):
- Latency: P50 reduced by ~9% and P95 reduced by ~14% on INT8 fused models with typical chat-turn length of 16 tokens
- Throughput: token/sec increased by ~7% at 99th percentile under steady batching
- Cost: estimated per-token memory bandwidth reduced ~11% for workloads with ≥20% cold-block density

Release notes: "Introduce token-adaptive dequantization and blockwise kernel sparsifier to reduce latency and memory bandwidth for quantized (INT8/FP8) inference. Opt-in via runtime flag 'runtime.dequant.token_adaptive=true'. Backwards-compatible KV metadata extension; no model changes required."

Operational notes and rollout plan:
- Feature disabled by default; enable behind a feature flag for a subset of customers/runtimes
- Start with A/B canary (5% traffic) and monitor block_quality, token_latency P95, and error-rate regressions
- If regressions detected, scheduler hint can route problematic requests to fallback lanes that always use the fused dequant path
- Add a smoothing threshold config and a per-tenant override to tune sensitivity to block sparsity

Additional remarks:
- This PR intentionally keeps the policy heuristics pluggable; next steps include an ML-based classifier in ENG-4210 that can replace the heuristic scorer, and a follow-up kernel patch that supports mixed precision within a block for further gains.
- No breaking API changes; KV metadata addition is optional and server-side-only, older nodes ignore the optional field.
